content:
The test image shows open soybean pods with seeds inside. Key observations:
- Left pod half: shriveled/cracked seed with darkening, appears deteriorated
- Right pod half: one seemingly normal yellowish seed and one discolored/mottled seed with dark spots
- Seeds appear shrunken and abnormal
- Some whitish material visible in pod interior

Top candidates: **Phomopsis** (cracked/shriveled seeds with chalky white mold), **Downy_mildew** (dried whitish fungal mass inside pod), **White_Mold** (smaller, lighter seeds).

The Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus reference image (top-right panel) shows a critical match — an open soybean pod with one lighter seed and one heavily dark-mottled seed, essentially identical to the test image's right pod.

**Analysis:**
- Test image right pod: one normal yellow seed + one seed with heavy dark/black mottling extending from the hilum — exactly matches BPMV's "diffusion of pigments from the seed hilum, resulting in mottling of the seed coat"
- Test image left pod: shrunken, poorly developed seed — consistent with "mottling is associated with poor germination"
- The BPMV reference collage (top-right) shows the exact same scene: split pod with one pale seed and one heavily mottled dark seed

Phomopsis shows cracked/shriveled seeds with chalky white mold — the chalky white mold is absent here. The dark mottling pattern from the hilum is the defining feature matching BPMV.
